title: cross-functional-roadmap-sync-prep-may-2026-olivia-personal-notes-draft
content:
Meeting: Cross-functional roadmap alignment (Product + Eng + Applied ML) - prep notes and follow-ups
Date: 2026-05-05 (sync) -- prepping notes here for runbook and talking points
Owner (prep): Olivia Chen
Attendees to invite: Maya (Product), Raj (Applied ML), Dylan (Serving Runtime), John (Infra), Asha (Console / Rollouts)

Goal: align on Q3 priorities that affect the inference runtime, model onboarding/variants, and product rollouts. We need clear tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs quality), owners, and acceptance criteria so product can finalize the hosted API and Dedicated marketing material by 2026-06-15.

Agenda (30-45m)
- Quick context + constraints (5m): Q2 learnings (high request churn; two major outages tied to routing fallback), observed latency/cost targets from pilot customers.
- Prioritized roadmap items that cross teams (20m):
  1) Model variant routing + automatic fallback (INF-1423) - product uses will expect 99% availability with graceful degradation to smaller quantized variant; eng must define compatibility matrix.
  2) Quantization profile standardization (OPT-871) - applied-ml proposing two canonical quantization profiles (8-bit and 4-bit) for initial rollout and recommended eval thresholds.
  3) Prefix/KV cache improvements and eviction policy - infra capacity implications and telemetry hooks for product (per-route cache hit rate).
  4) Eval & regression gating for rollouts - who owns prompt sets and automated checks tied to canary metrics.
- Acceptance criteria and metrics (10m): latency p50/p95, cost/token delta, quality regressions (ROUGE/BERTScore/paired-human checks), error-rate SLO.
- Timeline & owners (5m): commit for rollouts and customer beta windows.

Prep notes (my mental draft of talking points)
- Context: several hosted API customers hit higher-than-expected latency during peak due to model mismatches; fallback triggered but produced lower-quality outputs and product rollback cost us retention in one trial. Need both faster fallback decisioning and stronger quality guardrails.
- Product asks: deterministic fallback behavior, product-visible flags to prefer quality vs latency, and per-customer policy overrides. Also wants a simple way to advertise available model variants on hosted catalog.
- Eng realities: routing fallbacks currently implemented as static policy (latency threshold -> variant). We'll need a compatibility map for each model (tokenizer compatibility, context length, supported kv-cache layout). Generating this map will be work across model onboarding (applied-ml + eng). Estimates: ~2-3 engineer-weeks per common model family (Llama-2/3, Mistral/Redwood-verified variants).
- Applied-ML: quantization teams prefer to ship two profiles: 8-bit (safest) and 4-bit (aggressive). They propose target quality drop <= 3% on auto-eval sets for 4-bit and <=1% for 8-bit. Also propose per-customer fallback to 8-bit from 4-bit when quality checks fail in canary. Need eng to support runtime flags to force/override quantization per request.
- Observability: product needs per-route cost breakdown (tokenized input vs KV cache hits), per-variant p50/p95, and canary diff dashboards (quality metric vs baseline). Eng: add 3 new traces: variant_selected, cache_hit_flag, quant_profile_used.

Open questions to resolve in meeting
- Can we standardize the compatibility matrix format so product can render it in the catalog (JSON schema needed)? Who owns the schema? (proposal: applied-ml authors example, eng validates)
- What is the rollback policy if a canary shows quality regression > threshold? Auto-rollback or human-in-the-loop? (Product prefers auto with notification for customer tiers that opt-in)
- Timeline: realistic ship dates for core infra changes (routing improvements + traces) vs model quantization gating.

Proposed timeline (rough)
- May 2026: finalize schema for compatibility matrix; infra to add variant/tracing hooks (Dylan + John) - 3w sprint.
- Jun 2026: applied-ml completes quantization profiles and internal evals (Raj + Maya) - 2w intensive.
- Late Jun / Early Jul 2026: internal canary for 2 pilot customers (Product & SRE) - 2w.
- By 2026-07-15: begin broader beta on hosted API catalog (marketing & docs prep)

Acceptance criteria (draft)
- Routing/fallback: p99 availability maintained, fallback latency contribution to end-to-end request <= 20ms added on average.
- Quality: 4-bit quant profile <= 3% auto-eval drop on standard prompt set; 8-bit <= 1%.
- Observability: per-route dashboards with cache hit rate, variant distribution, and canary diffs available within 24 hours of canary start.

Action items (concrete)
- Olivia: share this prep doc + proposed agenda with attendees and Slack thread (#prod-eng-roadmap) by 2026-05-03. (DONE)
- Dylan: prepare short runbook for current fallback implementation and quick list of compatibility gaps by 2026-05-07.
- Raj: run quantization evals for top 3 models (Llama-3-8k, Redwood-v1, Mistral-medium) and post results to Confluence INF page by 2026-05-10. (JIRA-OPT-871 attached)
- Maya: draft product-level fallback UX and policy options (auto vs manual rollback, customer tiering) by 2026-05-11 and link to JIRA-INF-1423.
- John: estimate infra cost impact of caching changes (expected infra delta for Dedicated pools) and provide capacity numbers for pilot customers by 2026-05-12.
- Asha: update Console rollouts doc to include new telemetry fields and canary diff visuals by 2026-05-15.
- All: review compatibility matrix schema RFC (I will post a first pass) and comment inline by 2026-05-09.

Notes to self (informal / scratch)
- Keep meeting tight: prioritize decisions over complete spec. If compatibility schema needs more time, capture as follow-up with clear owner.
- Be ready to push back on auto-rollback if eng says risk of cascading rollbacks is high; propose safe default: auto-rollback for low-tier customers, human-in-loop for enterprise.
- Ask applied-ml for example evaluation prompts used in the past so product can reason about QA coverage.

Quick links / references
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Roadmap+Q3+2026
- JIRA: INF-1423 (routing fallback), OPT-871 (quant profiles)
- GH PR for variant selection prototype: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/439
- Slack thread: #prod-eng-roadmap (pin the canary dashboard screenshot after meeting)

Post-meeting follow-up template (to send to attendees)
- Summary of decisions made (one-paragraph)
- List of action items with owners + dates (copy from above)
- Next sync: 2026-05-19 (two weeks) - tentative; confirm during meeting

Personal TODO after meeting
- Draft compatibility matrix RFC and include example for Llama-3 (Olivia) - due 2026-05-09.
- Coordinate a short demo of runtime traces for Product (Dylan + Olivia) during the canary kickoff.

-- end of notes --
